groups.label: Existing ONT / router; AP feed pending
Passive data termination / route not selected

requirements: User selected ordinary wired switches now, with provision for future smart controls; no Hue system selected.
Main, soft and task describe functions, not cove shapes, fitting quantities, driver quantities or final ceiling positions.
One group can serve several fittings; preserve separate functional feeds until the designer and electrician agree the final grouping.

Bedroom main and soft groups should operate from entry and both bedsides. Three locations require a suitable multiway scheme, not three parallel ordinary switches. Confirm intermediate/two-way devices and interconnecting conductors locally.
Charging sockets stay available when bedroom lighting is off; fan control remains separate.
Conventional on/off switches give manual combinations, not preset dimming. No dimmer, smart relay or fan regulator compatibility is assumed.
Reserve practical backbox space, accessible junction/driver positions and spare containment; agree neutral availability for possible future modules without mixing circuits or backup supplies.
Board faces and module spans remain legacy illustrative envelopes, not a final switch/module purchase list.
Keep AC stabilizer, termination and isolation decisions deferred; a relationship to an indoor unit does not specify where its mains supply enters.
Qualified local design must establish circuits, protective devices, cable sizes, earthing, wet-area suitability and backup arrangements before installation.
drawing_limits: Dashed lines show control/service relationships only. They are not wires, conduit, appliance leads, safe routes or shared-circuit topology.
Lighting rings are functional-zone markers, not final fitting positions. Existing decorative ceiling remains a historical visualization only.
Equipment points are modeled body centers, not verified cable entry terminals. No lead-length or clearance conclusion can be taken from these lines.
Unresolved endpoints remain listed without invented geometry. Physical routing and visible-lead proposals need terminal/product and ceiling coordination.
